entries.name: Wake-sleep algorithm
entries.definition: An alternating learning procedure that trains a generative network from observed data and recognition-sampled hidden states during wake, and trains a recognition network from generative-model samples during sleep.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original wake-sleep procedure with separate generative and recognition parameters. It is a training algorithm for a paired probabilistic model, distinct from the Helmholtz-machine architecture, exact EM, joint ELBO-gradient training in NVIL, and reweighted wake-sleep. The original binary-sigmoid construction supplies local delta rules; the general phase distinction does not require every later model variant to use those same units. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 340 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 24 and 24 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: NVIL method distinctions, source-reading scopes, prior reviews and the carried wake-sleep discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Recognition samples are exact for q, not necessarily the model posterior. The generative wake update need not be an unbiased marginal-likelihood gradient or even have the same direction; a curator binary example demonstrates this distinction.

The sleep input distribution is the current model distribution rather than the empirical data distribution. Poor model samples can therefore allocate recognition capacity differently from data-conditioned training.

The original recognition distribution factors within each layer conditional on the preceding layer. This can miss explaining-away dependencies in the posterior; it does not assert unconditional independence of every hidden variable across layers.

The original paired-model sources explicitly do not establish a common descent objective for both phases. Exact posterior recovery, global convergence and monotonic likelihood improvement are not guaranteed.
Local binary-sigmoid rules depend on the stated conditional parameterization. No biological implementation, author-code execution or benchmark advantage is certified.

claims.statement: During wake, present an observed input and sample its hidden representation layer by layer through the bottom-up recognition distribution q_phi(h|x). Hold recognition parameters fixed for this update and ascend log p_theta(x,h) in the generative parameters. For the original Bernoulli-sigmoid units, a generative weight receives a learning-rate-scaled product of its sampled parent state and the difference between the sampled target state and the generative activation probability; biases use a constant parent. During sleep, sample a full configuration (x,h) ancestrally from the current top-down generative model, then ascend log q_phi(h|x) in the recognition parameters while holding generative parameters fixed. The generated lower-layer states serve as inputs and their known sampled upper-layer causes as targets. This also gives local Bernoulli delta rules in the original parameterization. The wake update follows the generative-parameter variational-bound gradient at fixed q; the sleep update instead fits recognition on model-generated inputs and targets the posterior-to-recognition KL direction averaged under model inputs. The two phases are not generally gradients of the same data ELBO.

entries.definition: A hierarchical probabilistic neural model that pairs a top-down generative model with a separately parameterized bottom-up recognition model approximating the distribution of hidden causes given observed input.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the original paired generative/recognition model family in Dayan and colleagues’ paper. Its original layered binary construction admits both a deterministic mean-field-inspired training approximation and a stochastic wake-sleep procedure; the architecture is not synonymous with either training rule. The generative and recognition parameters are separate, rather than tied symmetric connections of a Boltzmann machine. Related later variational autoencoders and deep belief networks are not treated as identity aliases. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 340 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 24 and 24 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: NVIL method distinctions, source-reading scopes, prior reviews and the carried wake-sleep discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. limitations: The tractable recognition family need not contain the true posterior, even when the directed generative model factors locally. Explaining-away dependencies can obstruct exact posterior matching.

The deterministic substitution of mean activations is an additional approximation, not exact evaluation of every nonlinear expectation in the stochastic model. The exact free-energy identity does not validate all approximation formulas or practical training updates.

Wake-sleep is a training option, and its sleep recognition step is not generally the data-ELBO gradient. A shared variational motivation does not establish a single objective decreased by all model variants.

The inspected author manuscript’s Equation (16) prints negative free energy as a positive sum of Bernoulli KL terms, conflicting with the preceding sign convention. The curated identity uses the explicit Section 2 decomposition; Appendix B derivative implementation was not audited and that printed approximate formula is not adopted.

The record describes a reusable architecture family, not a trained density estimator or a verified biological explanation. No exact posterior, universal compression gain or empirical ranking is asserted.

claims.statement: A top-down directed model p_theta(x,h) assigns probabilities to observed inputs and hidden configurations; a separately parameterized bottom-up model q_phi(h|x) produces a tractable approximate posterior. In the original layered binary construction, unit states in a layer are conditionally independent given the adjacent driving layer, with independent top-layer generative priors. Recognition proceeds through an acyclic bottom-up pass. The variational free energy is E_q[log q(h|x)-log p(x,h)], and log p(x) equals its negative plus KL(q(h|x)||p(h|x)); the negative free energy is therefore a lower bound under the normalized-model and support conditions. The paper describes stochastic recognition samples and, separately, a deterministic approximation that substitutes recognition means for sampled binary activities and neglects associated correlations. Its stochastic training alternative uses wake-sleep. The generative conditional need not be sigmoid: Appendix A considers noisy-or and other imaging rules. These choices do not change the defining presence of distinct generative and recognition models.

entries.name: Reweighted wake-sleep
entries.definition: A learning procedure for paired generative and inference networks that uses multiple inference samples and normalized importance weights for generative-model updates, with recognition updates from importance-weighted observed-data samples, model-generated sleep samples, or both.
entries.identity_notes: This is Bornschein and Bengio’s ICLR 2015 RWS procedure, scoped to its tractable joint/proposal calculations and Algorithm 1. It is distinct from ordinary wake-sleep, the generic importance-sampling identity, BBVI score-function ELBO optimization, and the choice of SBN or NADE component architecture. A single generative wake sample recovers the original wake model update; reproducing original wake-sleep additionally uses the sleep recognition update. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 340 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 24 and 24 lines respectively. All 17 unique matched line contents were inspected in full: NVIL method distinctions, source-reading scopes, prior reviews and the carried wake-sleep discovery lead, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Importance estimation requires proposal support wherever the target joint is positive, accessible joint/proposal values and suitable integrability. Arbitrary directed or deep-belief models with unavailable joint normalization are not covered merely by their architecture name.

The likelihood average can be unbiased while its logarithm and normalized-weight gradient remain biased at finite K. A consistent limit under suitable conditions is not an assertion of monotonic finite-K variance or bias improvement, global convergence, or exact posterior inference.

A proposal equal to the posterior makes likelihood weights constant, but it does not automatically minimize the variance of every model-gradient estimator. Poor proposal coverage can concentrate weights and make the estimate unreliable.

The recognition wake and sleep options optimize posterior-to-recognition matching under different input distributions. Neither is automatically the recognition gradient of the standard data ELBO used by NVIL, and differentiating an importance-weighted bound with respect to proposal parameters is a different update.

The main-text prose reverses the arguments of q in one loss expression, while Equations (4)–(5) and Algorithm 1 consistently use q(h|x). Supplement Equation (11) begins with a joint-weighted expression before introducing a conditional normalization; Equation (12) gives the intended posterior-KL target. This record follows those explicit update formulas and does not certify the printed intermediate equalities or author implementation.
K, component layers and update options are method choices rather than a universal best configuration. No benchmark advantage, author-code execution or runtime scaling claim is included.

claims.statement: For an observed input x and fixed current parameters, draw K independent latent configurations h_k from the recognition distribution q_phi(h|x), evaluate p_theta(x,h_k) and q_phi(h_k|x), and compute weights w_k=p_theta(x,h_k)/q_phi(h_k|x). Normalize them by their positive sum. Update theta using the weighted average of grad_theta log p_theta(x,h_k). The unnormalized average of w_k estimates p_theta(x); taking its logarithm gives a distinct, generally biased log-likelihood estimator. For recognition training, the wake option uses the same normalized weights to average grad_phi log q_phi(h_k|x), targeting KL(p_theta(h|x)||q_phi(h|x)) on observed inputs. The sleep option samples a fresh (x-prime,h-prime) from p_theta and ascends log q_phi(h-prime|x-prime). Algorithm 1 permits either recognition option or both. These displayed updates weight log-probability scores evaluated at sampled states; they do not differentiate through the normalized weights as an extra part of that score update. With K=1 the model update becomes the ordinary generative wake update, while the wake recognition score alone has zero expectation under normalized q at fixed parameters, as a curator consequence of the score identity.

claims.statement: For fixed observed x and joint model p(x,z), choose a variational family q(z;lambda), sample z from q, and maximize L(lambda)=E_q[log p(x,z)-log q(z;lambda)] by stochastic ascent. The mean-field version factors q into q_i(z_i;lambda_i) and uses for each factor the model log terms that depend on z_i together with -log q_i; unrelated terms cancel in expectation under the stated factorization. For parameter coordinate d in factor i, let h_d be the score and f_d be that score times the local log signal. A fixed control-variate coefficient gives f_d-a_d*h_d because E[h_d]=0; the population variance-minimizing coefficient is Cov(f_d,h_d)/Var(h_d) when these quantities exist and Var(h_d)>0. native_neighbors.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that repeatedly draws a coordinate or block from its full conditional distribution given the current values of the remaining coordinates.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes exact conditional resampling, including fixed coordinate cycles and fixed random-scan mixtures. It is a sampling procedure, not a Gibbs distribution, Markov random field, annealing schedule or conditional maximization method. Metropolis-within-Gibbs replaces some exact conditional draws by invariant transitions and is represented separately. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 159 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive full-checkout searches found prior discovery leads for Gibbs and slice sampling plus unrelated environment substring hits, not existing concept records. Existing HMM/MRF models and general Metropolis–Hastings were inspected to distinguish model, general transition and specialized algorithm scope.
limitations: The full conditional distributions must be compatible with a proper joint target and be sampled correctly. An approximate conditional draw is not automatically an exact Gibbs step.
Target invariance alone does not establish irreducibility, aperiodicity, convergence from every start or rapid mixing. Coordinate dependence and disconnected support can obstruct exploration.

The finite positive-state convergence theorem in Geman and Geman has explicit site-visit and positivity assumptions; it is not a theorem for every continuous, constrained or parallel Gibbs implementation.
Simultaneously updating dependent coordinates using stale neighbors is outside the stated sequential mechanism; valid parallel or adaptive scan schemes need separate arguments.
Fixed-temperature posterior sampling and a cooling schedule for optimization are different procedures. No universal convergence rate or image-restoration performance is asserted.

Later steps in a sweep use the values already updated earlier in that sweep. Exact conditional draws do not make the resulting successive joint states independent.

native_neighbors.name: Rejection sampling
native_neighbors.definition: A random-variate generation algorithm that draws proposals from a normalized envelope dominating an unnormalized target and accepts each with the target-to-envelope ratio, yielding independent target draws with fresh independent random trials.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is ordinary accept-reject generation with a valid global envelope. A rejected candidate is discarded, not recorded as a repeated chain state. The method differs from Metropolis acceptance, rejection-driven Metropolis proposals, importance weighting and selective filtering of model answers. The inspected primary source presents the scalar density case. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 167 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Existing Gibbs, Metropolis-within-Gibbs, random-walk and independence Metropolis mechanisms were inspected to resolve specialization boundaries.
limitations: A valid dominating envelope and an exact sampler for its normalized distribution are required. Clipping an invalid envelope ratio at one does not preserve the intended independent-sample law.
An envelope with excessive mass can make acceptance rare. No universal efficiency, dimensional scaling or bound on the number of trials is claimed.
The optional squeezing bound must be valid everywhere it is used; it is an evaluation shortcut, not a replacement target.
Numerical approximation, finite precision and inaccurate envelope sampling can change the output distribution. Log concavity is not required by ordinary rejection sampling itself.

claims.statement: For a nonnegative target g with finite positive integral, choose an integrable envelope g_u with g_u(x)≥g(x) everywhere on the target support and sample x from g_u/integral(g_u). Independently draw w uniformly on (0,1); accept x if w≤g(x)/g_u(x), otherwise discard the trial and repeat. An optional lower bound 0≤g_l≤g allows early acceptance when the same w≤g_l(x)/g_u(x), avoiding evaluation of g. Fresh independent trials produce independent accepted draws from normalized g. The target normalizing constant is not required for the acceptance ratio.

native_neighbors.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
native_neighbors.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is Kool and colleagues’ 2020 general ancestral algorithm. It extends the 2019 stochastic beam sampler beyond a fixed sequence-layer schedule: serial expansion is best-first, while expanding the whole retained frontier yields the stochastic-beam specialization. The generic categorical Gumbel-Top-k identity remains a separate mathematical method. Equal output distributions across expansion schedules do not make those schedules or their computational costs identical. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 331 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 11 and 11 lines respectively. All 10 unique hit contents were inspected: neighboring Gumbel-Top-k contrasts, saved review and ledger references, new source leads, and incidental concrete-distribution wording in an older random-search report, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The guarantee concerns finite discrete Bayesian networks with accessible normalized conditionals, well-defined positive support and the specified conditional-max construction. Arbitrary graphical models, cyclic dependencies or invalid zero-mass arithmetic are not silently covered.

The frontier contains disjoint surviving completion domains; after pruning it need not cover the entire original domain. Reusing overlapping partial assignments or sampling a variable before its parents violates the stated construction.

Serial m=1 expansion and full-frontier expansion can have the same sampling law but different work and parallel depth. The paper’s cost accounting includes allocated processor slots, idle slots and potentially unnecessary expansions; it is not a universal wall-clock speedup or a cost independent of variable-domain size.

The retained frontier bound counts entries, not all memory for model states, temporary children, assignments or result storage. Finite precision, ties and numerical stability need implementation policies.
The pseudocode’s access to the first queue element requires an empty-queue guard in an executable implementation. No literal pseudocode, author implementation or numerical benchmark was run.

Without-replacement configurations are dependent samples. The method’s sampling law does not make an arbitrary unweighted estimator unbiased, and it is distinct from Gibbs transitions or ordinary envelope-based rejection sampling.

claims.statement: Given a finite discrete Bayesian DAG with normalized parent-conditioned probabilities, choose a requested k no larger than the positive-probability configuration support and a parallel expansion budget m between 1 and the initial k. Start a priority frontier at the empty assignment, with log mass zero and a Gumbel root maximum sampled from Gumbel(0) or conditioned to zero. Each retained partial assignment represents a disjoint set of possible completions and carries their maximum perturbed log probability. Remove up to m highest-priority entries. Keep already-complete entries unchanged; for each incomplete entry choose an unassigned variable whose parents have been assigned, form all of its possible-value children, and update each child’s log mass with that variable’s conditional log probability. Sample child Gumbel maxima conditionally on their maximum equaling the parent score, using the source’s conditional-maximum transform. Combine children and retained entries with the unexpanded frontier, then keep at most the remaining requested count of highest-priority entries. Emit a completed assignment only while it is at the head of the priority frontier, decrementing the remaining sample count for every emitted assignment. Continue until the requested ordered sample has been returned. The pruning proof uses disjoint completion sets and consistent maxima to preserve the same ordered Gumbel-Top-k distribution as explicit enumeration of all configurations.

evidence.locator: Sections2.1 and2.4, PDF/printed pp.3 and5; Sections3.1–3.9, Equation(18), Lemmas1–2, Theorem3 and Algorithm1, pp.6–15

claims.statement: With m=1 and a fixed variable order the algorithm expands the highest-priority incomplete configuration first and can emit samples incrementally. Expanding the full retained frontier reproduces the layerwise stochastic-beam schedule under the fixed-order setup. The exact without-replacement distribution is preserved across the allowed scheduling choices, but total expansions and allocated processor work can differ.

claims.statement: A globally fixed topological order is sufficient but not required. Such a strategy changes the configuration tree and potential reuse/pruning while retaining the target distribution under the described construction.

Let P_theta(x,h) be the generative joint model and Q_phi(h|x) an inference-network distribution that can be sampled and evaluated efficiently. For each observed x, maximize the bound E_Q[log P_theta(x,h)-log Q_phi(h|x)]. Draw latent samples from Q. The raw model-gradient estimator averages d log P_theta(x,h)/d theta; the raw inference-gradient estimator averages the learning signal l=log P_theta(x,h)-log Q_phi(h|x) times d log Q_phi(h|x)/d phi. Its score expectation is zero, so baselines independent of the current latent sample conditional on x can be subtracted without changing the raw gradient expectation. The method fits an input-dependent neural baseline and maintains a scalar running center. It also divides the centered signal by max(1,sqrt(v)), where v is a running variance estimate, to adapt the update scale. In the supplement’s concrete minibatch ordering, subtract the input baseline, compute batch signal mean and variance, update the running center and variance using those batch statistics, then form centered/scaled inference updates and baseline updates; the model gradient remains unweighted by this signal. For layered factorizations, local learning signals omit terms that are independent of the relevant sampled descendants under the conditional score expectation, with separate baselines and variance estimates. The supplementary algorithm first samples the minibatch and computes baseline-adjusted learning signals, then updates the running mean and variance from that same minibatch before using them to center and scale its inference gradients. This practical order is distinct from the main-text identity for a baseline independent of the sampled latent value. The inference network is trained from observations and its own latent samples toward the variational objective. The source contrasts this with wake-sleep’s recognition update from model-generated samples and with pathwise gradients for continuous-variable variational methods. These distinctions do not make NVIL synonymous with every use of REINFORCE. Limits: A sample from Q is exact for Q while posterior inference remains approximate unless Q matches the model posterior. The variational-family capacity and optimization outcome affect the gap to the marginal log likelihood. Unbiasedness of the raw score estimator and subtraction of a conditionally sample-independent baseline do not automatically certify the final adaptive update. The supplement updates running statistics with the same minibatch before applying them, and normalization changes the update scale. Current-batch centering can introduce finite-sample bias; no blanket unbiasedness claim is made for that full practical procedure. The input baseline is trained using a squared-signal objective, which the source explicitly distinguishes from maximum variance reduction that accounts for score magnitude. A learned baseline need not improve variance in every setting. The method needs tractable sampling and evaluation of Q, evaluation of the joint P and differentiable log-probability parameters. It does not require differentiating the sampled discrete latent value, but support, zero probabilities and differentiation-under-expectation conditions still matter. Local-signal simplifications require the stated conditional independences. Arbitrarily dropping latent-dependent log terms can change the expected gradient.
